answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 210 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The grove graph is validated at intake and the bridge frontier is published, and hence the ancestry of every answer is public, and kernel anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Every submission must name 4 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight.
